scope.text: Nature Climate Change publishes highly significant research on contemporary global climate change, including its nature, underlying causes, impacts, and wider implications for the economy, policy, society, and the world at large. It covers original research across natural and social sciences and encourages interdisciplinary synthesis. Palaeoclimate studies fit only when they shed significant new light on the nature, causes, or impacts of current climate change.

official_excerpts.text: the most significant and cutting-edge research on the nature, underlying causes or impacts of global climate change and its implications for the economy, policy

inclusions: Atmospheric, cryospheric, ecological, hydrological, oceanographic, and modelling research tied to contemporary climate change
Economics, policy, governance, health, communication, psychology, sociology, ethics, sustainability, and development in the climate-change context
Interdisciplinary natural- and social-science climate research
official_exclusions_or_boundaries: Palaeoclimate research that does not provide significant new insight into current climate change

official_excerpts.text: Article, Analysis, Brief Communication, Registered Report, Correspondence, Review, Perspective, Progress, Comment, Matters Arising, News and Views, Book & Arts Review, Feature

submission_notes: Article is a substantial novel research study; Analysis is a new or comparative analysis producing broad, arresting conclusions; Brief Communication is a concise high-quality study; Registered Report evaluates the importance of the question and rigour of methods before results are known.
Unsolicited Review, Perspective, and Progress proposals require a one-to-two-page synopsis through the submission system.
The marked non-primary types should not report previously unpublished primary findings and may contain only minimal new supporting data.
